mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 25 basis points within a month signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within two months signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within two months signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decrease by more than 100,000 in a month, it signals a severe labor market downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is negative, it signals a supply-side recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the signal.
